newsitem.title: USA: Universal Foods to move into non-food markets.
newsitem.headline: Universal Foods to move into non-food markets.

text.p: Universal Foods Corp said it planned to move aggressively into non-food markets in seeking opportunities for its color, flavor and Red Star bioproducts divisions.
"We will also continue to expand geographically in Europe and Asia/Pacific," Kenneth Manning, president, said in a statement.

On Thursday, Universal Foods reported operating earnings of $0.67 a share for the fourth quarter ended September 30, up from $0.63 in the year-earlier period. Including charges, the company earned $0.02 a share, down from $0.09.

The color division's revenues for fiscal 1996 rose 6.3 percent to $158.8 million on the strength of sales of domestic food and beverage colorings. The company said process technology improvements resulted in a breakthrough in the concentration and production of carminic acid, a natural red color that is soluble in water.

Revenue generated by the dehydrated products division for the year rose 12.9 percent to $132.2 million, bolstered by European acquisitions and U.S. onion and garlic sales. Operating profit improved significantly, to an unspecified level, due to strong demand and limited supply of U.S. chili products and improvements in European plant operations
In the flavor division, sales declined by 4.9 percent to $259.8 million, as softness in U.S. food and dairy flavors offset improvement in markets outside the United States and in U.S. beverages.
Red Star BioProducts revenues in the year rose 1.2 percent to $99.3 million, while operating income rose significantly because of a product mix shift.
